```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "area_report_helpers.R"))
X    <- readRDS(here::here("data", "area_mid_sussex.rds"))        # R/17_area_analysis.R
TR   <- readRDS(here::here("data", "trust_effects.rds"))          # R/19_trust_effects.R
DE   <- readRDS(here::here("data", "district_effects.rds"))       # R/18_district_effects.R
LADS <- readRDS(here::here("data", "sussex_lads.rds"))            # R/19b_sussex_boundaries.R
P    <- readRDS(here::here("data", "panel_data.rds"))
FOCUS <- "Mid Sussex"; WS <- "West Sussex"; BH <- "Brighton and Hove"
AREAS <- c(FOCUS, WS, BH)

S   <- X$schools
NAT <- X$national
latest <- X$latest_panel
abs_last <- tail(X$abs_years, 1)
GOV <- gov_table(X, TR, DE)

ap <- X$area_profile |> filter(year_label == latest)
prof <- X$profiles |> filter(year_label == latest)
p_ws <- prof |> filter(LANAME == WS); p_bh <- prof |> filter(LANAME == BH)

# Every district in England with at least five schools, to rank against
lp <- X$lad_profiles |> filter(year_label == latest, schools >= 5) |>
  mutate(r_att8 = rank(-att8), r_dis = rank(-att8_dis), r_gap = rank(-gap),
         r_fsm = rank(fsm), n = n())
lp_ms <- lp |> filter(lad == FOCUS)
lp_ws <- X$lad_profiles |> filter(year_label == latest, LANAME == WS)

dec   <- X$decomp
d_get <- function(la, g, comp) dec$points[dec$la == la & dec$group == g & dec$component == comp]
d_tot <- function(la, g) { x <- dec |> filter(la == !!la, group == g) |> slice(1); x$la_att8 - x$nat_att8 }
place <- function(la, g) d_get(la, g, "Region") + d_get(la, g, "Local authority effect")

ser  <- X$abs_series
s_at <- function(area, tp, col = "abs_rate") ser[[col]][ser$area == area & ser$time_period == tp]
rs <- X$reasons |> filter(time_period == abs_last)
rs_w <- rs |> select(area, reason, pp) |> pivot_wider(names_from = area, values_from = pp)
r_at <- function(area, r) rs_w[[area]][rs_w$reason == r]
exa <- X$excl$area; ex_last <- max(exa$time_period)
ex_at <- function(a, col = "susp_rate") exa[[col]][exa$la_name == a & exa$time_period == ex_last]

se <- DE$school_eff |> filter(URN %in% X$urns) |>
  select(SCHNAME, outcome, school_effect) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = school_effect)
se_at <- function(s, o) pct(se[[o]][grepl(s, se$SCHNAME)])
fe <- function(o, s) DE$focus |> filter(lad == FOCUS, outcome == o, spec == s)
S1 <- "With a school term"

js <- X$joint$schools |> filter(URN %in% X$urns)
sc <- X$scenarios

# Disadvantaged cohort sizes, the reason every disadvantaged figure here is noisy
coh <- P |> filter(as.integer(URN) %in% X$urns, year_label == latest) |>
  transmute(SCHNAME, cohort = TPUP, dis = TFSM6CLA1A)
va_s <- X$va |> group_by(school) |>
  summarise(all = mean(va_ATT8SCR), dis = mean(va_ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A),
            non = mean(va_ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A), years = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Draft for discussion

A first draft, written alongside the [East Sussex](east_sussex.html) and
[West Sussex](west_sussex.html) documents. Every figure comes from
published Department for Education data and the national models of
[How to Pull the Right Lever](https://adamdennett.github.io/school_attainment_tool/pulling_the_right_lever_v2.html).
Nothing uses pupil-level records.
:::

# Summary {.unnumbered}

**Mid Sussex is one of the most advantaged school districts in England,
and its disadvantaged pupils do not share in that advantage.** Its
`r nrow(S)` state secondary schools in Burgess Hill, Haywards Heath,
East Grinstead and Hassocks are mostly high-performing:

- **Overall results are high:** `r pts(ap$att8)` in Attainment 8 in
  `r latest`, `r ord(lp_ms$r_att8)` of `r lp_ms$n` districts in England
  with five or more schools.
- **Few pupils are disadvantaged:** `r pp(ap$fsm)`%, against
  `r pp(NAT$fsm)`% nationally.
- **Disadvantaged pupils average `r pts(ap$att8_dis)`**, below the
  national `r pts(NAT$att8_dis)` (`r ord(lp_ms$r_dis)` of `r lp_ms$n`).
- **The gap between the two groups is `r pts(ap$gap)` points**, the
  `r ord(lp_ms$r_gap)` widest of any district.

The other findings:

- **The model explains most of the overall advantage.** Low
  disadvantage, high prior attainment and good attendance lift
  Mid Sussex well above England. Its schools add a little more on top.
- **For disadvantaged pupils the picture reverses.** West Sussex's
  county-wide effect and the South East's regional effect cost them
  `r pts(-place(FOCUS, "Disadvantaged"))` points. Mid Sussex's schools
  then fall a further `r pts(-d_get(FOCUS, "Disadvantaged", "Unexplained (school residual)"))`
  points below expectation for these pupils, while sitting above
  expectation overall.
- **It is a school-level pattern, not a district one.** No Mid Sussex
  district effect can be found. Oathall and Warden Park are above
  expectation overall and well below for their disadvantaged pupils.
  Downlands is strong for both.
- **Attendance is good, but three schools run more absence than their
  intakes predict:** Imberhorne, Sackville and The Burgess Hill Academy.
  As in the rest of West Sussex, reduced timetables run at nearly twice
  the national rate.
- **Disadvantaged groups are small,** `r min(coh$dis)` to
  `r max(coh$dis)` pupils a year per school. Every school-level figure for
  them moves by several points from year to year and should be read over
  several years.

# About this analysis

Mid Sussex is a district of West Sussex, not a local authority, and that
shapes what can be said:

- **The national models place schools in local authorities.** The
  "local authority effect" in this document is West Sussex's, shared
  with every school in the county.
- **What is particular to Mid Sussex** shows up in its schools' own
  residuals, and in the district test of @sec-ms-effect.
- **Absence and exclusions** are summed over the district's seven
  schools, followed through any change of URN.

Everything else is as in the [East Sussex](east_sussex.html) and
[West Sussex](west_sussex.html) documents, which describe the methods in
full.

# The district's schools

```{r map}
#| fig-cap: "Mid Sussex's state-funded secondary schools, coloured by overall absence in 2024/25. Hover for figures and who runs each school; switch to the governance colouring at top right."
map_area(X, GOV, LADS, height = 460)
```

```{r school-table}
#| tbl-cap: "Every state-funded secondary school in Mid Sussex, 2024/25, with the size of its disadvantaged Year 11 group."
S |>
  left_join(coh |> select(SCHNAME, dis), by = "SCHNAME") |>
  arrange(TOWN, SCHNAME) |>
  transmute(School = SCHNAME, Town = TOWN,
            Type = ifelse(type == "Academy", "Academy", "Maintained"),
            Pupils = pupils, `FSM %` = round(fsm, 1),
            `Disadvantaged in Year 11` = dis,
            `Absence %` = round(absence, 1), `KS2` = round(ks2_c, 1),
            `Att 8` = round(att8, 1), `Att 8 disadv.` = round(att8_dis, 1),
            Ofsted = ofsted) |>
  kt(align = "llllrrrrrrl")
```

```{r gov-counts}
#| include: false
chg <- GOV |> filter(changed)
```

`r sum(GOV$trust_kind == "Maintained")` of the seven schools are
maintained by West Sussex County Council. The other three are academies:

- **Warden Park**, in the Sussex Learning Trust;
- **St Paul's Catholic College**, in the Bosco Catholic Education Trust;
- **The Burgess Hill Academy**, a sponsored academy that moved from the
  University of Brighton Academies Trust to the Sussex Learning Trust
  after 2024/25.

```{r fig-governance}
#| fig-cap: "Who ran each Mid Sussex school in 2024/25, and how far its results sat above or below the national model's expectation over 2021/22 to 2024/25."
#| fig-height: 4.5
fig_governance(GOV, "Mid Sussex's schools by who ran them in 2024/25")
```

# How Mid Sussex compares

```{r profile-table}
#| tbl-cap: "Mid Sussex against West Sussex, Brighton and Hove and England, 2024/25. Means of school-level figures."
row <- function(lab, col, d = 1) {
  f <- function(x) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), x)
  tibble(Measure = lab, `Mid Sussex` = f(ap[[col]]), `West Sussex` = f(p_ws[[col]]),
         `Brighton and Hove` = f(p_bh[[col]]),
         England = f(sum(prof[[col]] * prof$schools, na.rm = TRUE) /
                       sum(prof$schools[!is.na(prof[[col]])])))
}
bind_rows(
  row("Attainment 8, all pupils", "att8"),
  row("Attainment 8, disadvantaged", "att8_dis"),
  row("Attainment 8, non-disadvantaged", "att8_non"),
  row("Disadvantage gap (points)", "gap"),
  row("Disadvantaged (FSM6) %", "fsm"),
  row("Overall absence %", "absence"),
  row("Persistent absence %", "persistent"),
  row("Mean KS2 (centred)", "ks2_c", 2),
  row("EAL %", "eal")) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r fig-districts-ws}
#| fig-cap: "Attainment 8 for disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged pupils in West Sussex's seven districts, 2024/25, school means. The gap between the two is printed on each district's line."
#| fig-height: 4.6
lp_ws |>
  select(lad, att8_dis, att8_non, gap) |>
  mutate(lad = reorder(lad, att8_non)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = lad)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = att8_dis, xend = att8_non, yend = lad), colour = LIGHT, linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = att8_dis, colour = "Disadvantaged"), size = 3.4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = att8_non, colour = "Non-disadvantaged"), size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(aes(x = (att8_dis + att8_non) / 2, label = sprintf("%.1f", gap)),
            vjust = -0.9, size = 3, colour = GREY) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = NAT$att8_dis, linetype = "dotted", colour = PURPLE) +
  annotate("text", x = NAT$att8_dis, y = 0.6, label = "England, disadvantaged", hjust = -0.05,
           size = 3, colour = PURPLE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Disadvantaged = WARM, `Non-disadvantaged` = TEAL), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Attainment 8", y = NULL,
       title = "Mid Sussex has the county's best results and one of its widest gaps") +
  theme_note()
```

The gap is not one year's accident. It was
`r pts(X$area_profile$gap[X$area_profile$year_label == "2021-22"])` points
in 2021/22 and `r pts(max(X$area_profile$gap))` at its widest
(`r X$area_profile$year_label[which.max(X$area_profile$gap)]`). Mid
Sussex's non-disadvantaged pupils do better than England's every year,
and its disadvantaged pupils worse.

# What explains attainment in Mid Sussex

```{r fig-decomp}
#| fig-cap: "Why average Attainment 8 differs from England's, by factor, all school-years 2021/22 to 2024/25, for Mid Sussex, West Sussex and Brighton and Hove. Approximate Attainment 8 points; the pieces sum to the total in each panel."
#| fig-height: 9
fig_decomp(dec, AREAS, c("All pupils", "Disadvantaged"))
```

```{r decomp-table}
#| tbl-cap: "The decomposition for Mid Sussex, in Attainment 8 points. 'Place' is West Sussex's effect plus the South East's; 'unexplained' is what Mid Sussex's own schools add beyond everything the model accounts for."
decomp_table(dec, FOCUS)
```

**For all pupils**, Mid Sussex is `r pts(d_tot(FOCUS, "All pupils"))`
points above England. Almost all of that is intake, and the model
expects it:

- low disadvantage (+`r pts(d_get(FOCUS, "All pupils", "Disadvantage (% FSM)"), 2)`);
- high prior attainment (+`r pts(d_get(FOCUS, "All pupils", "Prior attainment (KS2)"), 2)`);
- good attendance (+`r pts(d_get(FOCUS, "All pupils", "Absence"), 2)`).

The district's schools add `r sgn(d_get(FOCUS, "All pupils", "Unexplained (school residual)"), 2)`
on top, more than enough to offset West Sussex's county-wide effect.

**For disadvantaged pupils** the picture reverses: Mid Sussex is
`r pts(-d_tot(FOCUS, "Disadvantaged"))` points *below* England.

- **Place** takes `r pts(-place(FOCUS, "Disadvantaged"), 2)`: West
  Sussex's own effect and the South East's.
- **The schools themselves** take a further
  `r pts(-d_get(FOCUS, "Disadvantaged", "Unexplained (school residual)"), 2)`.
  They are above expectation for their other pupils and below it for
  these.
- **Low disadvantage counts against them** too
  (`r pts(d_get(FOCUS, "Disadvantaged", "Disadvantage (% FSM)"), 2)`).

That last point is the Lever report's most contested finding showing up
locally. Across England, disadvantaged pupils do slightly better in
schools with more disadvantaged pupils, once everything else is
accounted for. The likely reason is that such schools organise around
them, and spend pupil premium on provision that a handful of pupils
cannot sustain. In Mid Sussex, where a school may have twenty
disadvantaged pupils in a year group, that does not happen at scale.

# The disadvantaged gap, school by school {#sec-ms-gap}

```{r fig-va-split}
#| fig-cap: "Each Mid Sussex school's value added for its disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged pupils, mean over the years available (2021/22 to provisional 2025/26). Above zero means better than the national model expects for similar pupils."
#| fig-height: 4.6
va_s |>
  pivot_longer(c(dis, non), names_to = "grp", values_to = "v") |>
  mutate(grp = recode(grp, dis = "Disadvantaged", non = "Non-disadvantaged"),
         school = reorder(school, v * (grp == "Non-disadvantaged"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(v, school, colour = grp)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
  geom_line(aes(group = school), colour = LIGHT, linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(size = 3.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Disadvantaged = WARM, `Non-disadvantaged` = TEAL), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Value added (Attainment 8 points)", y = NULL,
       title = "Several schools do well by most pupils and less well by their disadvantaged ones") +
  theme_note()
```

```{r va-split-notes}
#| include: false
gap_schools <- va_s |> filter(non > 0, dis < -1) |> arrange(dis)
```

`r nrow(gap_schools)` schools are above expectation for their
non-disadvantaged pupils and more than a point below it for their
disadvantaged ones: `r paste(gap_schools$school, collapse = ", ")`. With
each school's own record in the model:

- **Oathall Community College** is `r sgn(se_at("Oathall", "All pupils"))`%
  overall and `r sgn(se_at("Oathall", "Disadvantaged"))`% for
  disadvantaged pupils.
- **Warden Park** is `r sgn(se_at("Warden", "All pupils"))`% overall and
  `r sgn(se_at("Warden", "Disadvantaged"))`% for disadvantaged pupils.
- **Downlands Community School** is the exception, above expectation for
  both groups (`r sgn(se_at("Downlands", "All pupils"))`% and
  `r sgn(se_at("Downlands", "Disadvantaged"))`%). It has one of the
  district's smallest disadvantaged groups.

```{r tbl-dis-years}
#| tbl-cap: "Attainment 8 of each school's disadvantaged pupils, year by year (2025/26 provisional), with the size of the group in 2024/25. Small groups make single years unreliable."
X$va |>
  select(school, year_label, ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A) |>
  mutate(year_label = sub("-", "/", year_label)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year_label, values_from = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A) |>
  left_join(coh |> transmute(school = SCHNAME, `Disadvantaged pupils, 2024/25` = as.character(dis)),
            by = "school") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ifelse(is.na(.x), "", sprintf("%.1f", .x)))) |>
  rename(School = school) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrrr")
```

With groups this small, any one school-year can move by ten points.
Imberhorne and Sackville's disadvantaged results fell sharply in 2023/24
and recovered after. The pattern that matters is the one across years and
schools, and it is consistent: the district's disadvantaged pupils do
less well than its other pupils, by more than they do in similar schools
elsewhere.

# Is there a Mid Sussex effect? {#sec-ms-effect}

The district test of the [East Sussex document](east_sussex.html#sec-districts)
adds a district level to the national model, with and without each
school's own record.

```{r tbl-ms-effect}
#| tbl-cap: "The Mid Sussex district effect, over and above West Sussex's, with 95% intervals."
DE$focus |> filter(lad == FOCUS) |>
  transmute(Specification = spec, Outcome = outcome,
            `Effect (%)` = sprintf("%+.1f", pct(effect)),
            `95% interval` = sprintf("%+.1f to %+.1f", pct(ci_lo), pct(ci_hi)),
            Significant = ifelse(sig, "Yes", "No")) |>
  kt(align = "llrrl")
```

None of Mid Sussex's district effects can be told apart from zero on
either specification. The district's results are explained by its
intake, West Sussex's county effect and its individual schools, which
differ a good deal. Unlike Crawley, the
[West Sussex](west_sussex.html#sec-districts) district where every school
is below expectation, there is nothing that all Mid Sussex schools share.

```{r fig-school-effects}
#| fig-cap: "Each Mid Sussex school's own persistent effect, from the model with a school term: Attainment 8 for all pupils, and absence beyond what its intake predicts."
#| fig-height: 4
fig_school_effects(DE, X$urns, "Mid Sussex's schools differ more from each other than the district does from the county")
```

# Absence

```{r fig-abs-series}
#| fig-cap: "Overall absence, autumn and spring terms, 2016/17 to 2025/26. Sessions-weighted; 2019/20 not collected."
#| fig-height: 4.8
fig_abs_series(ser, AREAS, "Mid Sussex runs below England and West Sussex")
```

Attendance in Mid Sussex is good:

- **`r pp(s_at(FOCUS, abs_last))`% absence** in autumn and spring
  `r yr(abs_last)`, against `r pp(s_at("England", abs_last))`% for England
  and `r pp(s_at(WS, abs_last))`% for West Sussex.
- **Persistent absence** is `r pp(s_at(FOCUS, abs_last, "pa_rate"))`%.

The district's intake predicts lower absence still. Its schools run
`r sgn(X$area_excess$excess, 2)` points above what their pupils'
profiles predict, but the excess is concentrated in three schools:

```{r tbl-ms-absence}
#| tbl-cap: "Each school's absence against what its intake predicts, mean 2021/22 to 2024/25, and its reasons in the latest year (percentage of sessions)."
js |>
  select(URN, SCHNAME, obs_abs, exp_intake, excess_intake_pp) |>
  left_join(X$sch_reasons |> transmute(URN = as.integer(urn), illness, unauth_other, reduced, excluded),
            by = "URN") |>
  arrange(desc(excess_intake_pp)) |>
  transmute(School = SCHNAME, `Absence %` = round(obs_abs, 1),
            `Predicted by intake %` = round(exp_intake, 1),
            `Above prediction` = sprintf("%+.1f", excess_intake_pp),
            Illness = round(illness, 1), Unauthorised = round(unauth_other, 1),
            `Reduced timetable` = round(reduced, 2), Suspended = round(excluded, 2)) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrrrr")
```

- **The Burgess Hill Academy, Imberhorne and Sackville** each run more
  than a point above their predicted absence.
- **Oathall and St Paul's** run below theirs.

As across West Sussex, reduced timetables are used at about twice the
national rate: `r pp(r_at(FOCUS, "Reduced timetable"), 2)`% of sessions
against `r pp(r_at("England", "Reduced timetable"), 2)`%. Oathall's rate
is the highest in the district.

```{r tbl-scenario}
#| tbl-cap: "Predicted Attainment 8 gain if each school's absence fell to the national school average (2024/25). Indicative only."
scenario_table(sc)
```

Only three schools are above the national average absence, and the
gains from bringing them to it are modest: up to
`r pts(max(sc$gain_all))` points. Attendance is not Mid Sussex's lever.

**Suspensions** are well below the national rate:
`r pp(ex_at(FOCUS))` per 100 pupils in `r yr(ex_last)`, against
`r pp(ex_at("England"))` for England and `r pp(ex_at(WS))` for West
Sussex. The rate varies widely between schools:

```{r tbl-susp}
#| tbl-cap: "Suspensions per 100 pupils and permanent exclusions, by school, latest year."
X$excl_schools |> arrange(desc(susp_rate)) |>
  transmute(School = school_name, Pupils = headcount,
            `Suspensions per 100` = round(susp_rate, 1), `Permanent exclusions` = perm_excl) |>
  kt(align = "lrrr")
```

# Implications and questions for discussion

1. **The district's issue is its disadvantaged pupils, not its schools
   overall.** Mid Sussex's results are among the best of any district,
   and its disadvantaged pupils' results are below the national average.
   That combination is the question worth putting to its schools.
2. **Small numbers need a different approach.** With `r min(coh$dis)` to
   `r max(coh$dis)` disadvantaged pupils in a year group, the provision that serves them
   well in high-disadvantage schools cannot be built school by school.
   Seven schools within a few miles of each other might build it
   together.
3. **Learn from Downlands**, which does well by both groups, and ask
   what Oathall and Warden Park do differently for their disadvantaged
   pupils.
4. **The county effect still applies.** Mid Sussex's disadvantaged
   pupils carry West Sussex's below-expectation effect too. The county
   question in the [West Sussex document](west_sussex.html) applies here
   as well.
5. **Attendance and suspensions** are not the district's problem, with
   three schools' absence the exception. Reduced timetables, as across
   West Sussex, are worth a look.

# Notes on method {.unnumbered}

Methods and sources are those of the [East Sussex](east_sussex.html)
document. District membership comes from each school's postcode (ONS
postcode directory, via postcodes.io). Absence and exclusions for the
district are summed over its schools, including any predecessor URNs.
This document is built by `R/17_area_analysis.R`,
`R/18_district_effects.R`, `R/19_trust_effects.R` and `mid_sussex.qmd`.
